pl-l4d37c1-d1e115.summary: Turns to the other things that make persons wholly unlawful, and first order.

pl-l4d37c1-d1e118.summary: States that in some orders marriage can by no means be contracted, and if union occurs there is divorce: priesthood, diaconate, and subdiaconate; in others marriage is permitted, unless they have taken the religious habit or vowed continence.
claims: Minor orders permit marriage unless vowed.

pl-l4d37c1-d1e121.summary: Cites Pope Leo: the Roman Church permits clerics, lectors, porters, exorcists, and acolytes outside vow and habit who will not profess continence to marry a virgin, not a widow or divorced woman, since they cannot thereafter be promoted to the subdiaconate, nor can a layman who married a non-virgin or a bigamist become a cleric.
claims: Minor clerics may marry a virgin but cannot then advance.

pl-l4d37c1-d1e128.summary: Cites the Council of Carthage: bishops, priests, deacons, and subdeacons must abstain from their wives, or be removed from ecclesiastical office; other clerics are not compelled.
claims: Clerics in major orders must abstain from their wives.

pl-l4d37c1-d1e137.summary: Adds Leo: the law of continence is the same for altar ministers as for bishops and priests; as laymen or lectors they could lawfully marry, but on reaching these grades what was lawful ceased to be lawful.
claims: Continence binds from ordination to major orders.

pl-l4d37c1-d1e143.summary: Cites the Sixth Synod: whoever approaching the clergy wishes to marry should do so before the order of subdeacon.
claims: Clerics must marry before the subdiaconate.

pl-l4d37c1.summary: Turns to impediments that make persons wholly unlawful, first order. In priesthood, diaconate, and subdiaconate marriage cannot be contracted, and if union occurs there is divorce; in other orders marriage is allowed unless one has taken the religious habit or vowed continence. Leo permits lower clerics outside vow and habit to marry a virgin, not a widow or divorcee, though they cannot then be promoted to the subdiaconate. Carthage requires bishops, priests, deacons, and subdeacons to abstain from wives; Leo says the law of continence binds altar ministers once ordained; the Sixth Synod requires clerics who wish to marry to do so before the subdiaconate.
claims: Major orders are a diriment impediment to marriage.
Lower clerics may marry a virgin but cannot then advance.
Clerics in major orders must abstain from their wives.
